cells.tense: You're here with the pen, and what you imagine now comes from everything you've already lived through.
cells.ask: Offer one goal the feeling has already picked, and let it pull you a step past what you can see.
cells.core:
You're in the room with what's in front of you, and you picture from it. Nothing you make needs defending, because it came out of something real. You get enough light for the next step, never the whole road, and that's fine by you. People can stand on what you describe.

The next thing this balance can feed is forward motion. There's a goal you already feel in your body, not one you reasoned your way into. Give it a destination and let the wanting carry you the first stretch. The picture doesn't have to be finished for you to move toward it.
cells.sheetLine: Your dreams are built from what you've lived, and they're ready to be walked.
cells.verb: trusting the path that reveals itself
cells.place: in the clearing you keep by letting go

cells.tense: You're pushing ahead into a future you can't write yet, bracing for a picture only you can see.
cells.ask: Tend one thing that's actually growing today, and leave the outcome alone for now.
cells.core:
The picture stays a picture when this is working. You hold it loosely, you see what's here as well as what could be, and the vision serves the day instead of replacing it. The dreaming and the living share a room.

Lately the reverse. The imagination has run ahead of what's real. What you picture feels like what's happening, so you keep living in a version of events that hasn't arrived, and the people around you can't find you in it. Holding on harder doesn't make the picture truer. It makes it heavier.

Care that doesn't exhaust is the way back. Choose one thing that's genuinely growing — a person, a project, a slow skill — and give it conditions, not a deadline. Then let it be.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in the picture instead of living with it.

cells.tense: Something in you already changed the record and moved on, but part of you is still standing where you were.
cells.ask: Name one thing you already know to be true before you can explain why, and let it count.
cells.core:
This runs on a quiet sense of what matters when it's whole. A feeling arrives, you follow it, and the why shows up later — or never. You can sit with the not-knowing, and the depth underneath the surface is there when you want it.

The surface is where you are now. A hunch arrives and gets dismissed before it can land, so everything has to be argued into existence — and most of it can't be. The symbols and dreams that used to mean something have gone quiet, and you call it being realistic. Realism was never the issue. Letting the not-knowing be enough was.

You don't get the depth back by trying harder at it. Give your direct perception one thing to sit with, one thing you recognize as mattering without a case built for it. Then let that recognition stand. It carries its own weight, and you can live on it.
cells.sheetLine: You already know what matters. Letting yourself say so is what's missing.
cells.verb: trusting the path that reveals itself

cells.tense: You're still writing in a room you've already left, and the pages keep filling either way.
cells.ask: Sit with one small practice for a week and watch what it shows you about the life you're steering.
cells.core:
Focused and quiet, that's what this is when it's whole. You keep one small practice because it works, not because it should, and what you refine gets sharper without the refinement eating the living. Solitude here connects you to something rather than cutting you off from it.

As it stands you're doing things — showing up, saying things that land harder than you mean, picturing a life you never named — and talking about all of it as if it just happens. What you imagine for yourself shapes the days you step into, whether or not you'd call it yours to shape. The record is being kept. You're just not admitting you hold the pen.

Pick one small thing and make it a repeated practice: same time, same way, a few minutes. Do it mostly alone. A steady, unflashy light kept lit by attention shows you what you're already aiming at, and from there the aim can be yours.
